text:
Maya: Heads-up — onboarding call with Horizon Health next week. They want a 99.9% availability SLA and a committed throughput number for eu-west. Need a quick mapping from SLA / p95 latency targets -> committed GPU pool sizing we can sell.
Sam: Do we have their expected peak RPS and avg seq len? those drive tokens/s which matters for GPU throughput.
Maya: They provided: peak 120 rps sustained for 10m windows, p95 gen latency target 350ms, avg tokens per request 220, KV cache hit ~35%.
Devin: Quick convert: tokens/sec = rps * tokens_per_request. So 120 * 220 = 26,400 tokens/s. With 35% cache hit that's ~17,160 effective tokens/s to compute.
Ira: But GPU throughput depends on model & batch profile. For gpt-ish baseline we use our "tokens_per_gpu_sec" metric — for v1-std we model ~2,400 tokens/sec per GPU at 1k context with our kernel set and avg batch sizes.
Sam: So naive GPUs = 17,160 / 2,400 = ~7.15 -> round up to 8 GPUs. But that ignores P99 bursts and cold-cache tails. Also need headroom for autoscale stabilization and network variance.
Maya: Right. Sales wants a committed pool (no autoscale) that guarantees throughput within SLA. We should propose a commit floor + burst buffer. Recommend 10 committed GPUs + burst via on-demand for 2 hours/day? Thoughts.
Devin: Suggest we compute three bands: floor (sustained), SLA headroom (to meet p95 under 99th percentile sequence length & KV miss), and burst (short spikes). Example calc I did quickly: 
```
Sustained_tokens = 120 * 220 * (1 - 0.35) = 17,160
Model_tokens_per_gpu = 2400 (v1-std baseline)
Sustained_gpus = ceil(17160 / 2400) = 8
SLA_headroom_factor = 1.25 (accounts for seq length variance + mmapped latency) -> 8 * 1.25 = 10
Burst_buffer = 0.25 * SLA_headroom -> 2.5 -> round to 3
Recommended_commit = 10 GPUs, allow burst to 13 GPUs
```
Sam: That matches intuition. We should annotate assumptions: model variant, batch shaping, average concurrency per connection, and that KV hit rate could improve with prewarming.
Ira: Also add regional capacity constraints — eu-west inventory often has fewer spare A100s; if customer wants hard commit we need to anchor a calendar slot and a replacement plan. For commits we usually give a 72-hour notice window for maint/evacuation and a cross-region fallback option.
Maya: Good call. Sales will ask about cost delta between commit vs on-demand. Can someone rough a monthly cost delta for 10 vs 13 GPUs (A10G equiv)?
capacity-bot: Estimated monthly cost delta (region eu-west):
- 10 committed GPUs: $28,500/month (committed discount applied)
- Allow burst to 13 (3 on-demand): marginal on-demand cost for burst capacity = ~$9,000/month if used continuously, but expected only for short windows -> effective cost ~= $1,200/month based on 2 hours/day average.
Devin: Add a note: if their usage profile has fat tails (10% days with +2x traffic) commit + reserved burst isn't enough, we should propose an SLO-based credit or graded fallback (reduce fidelity model when overloaded).
Sam: Implementation detail: when sizing commit we must tie it to an ingress policy that reserves concurrency slots on each GPU across the pool. We'll need to pin their pool to a dedicated subnet and mark nodes with customer tag for billing reconciliation.
Maya: I'll draft a one-pager for sales with the math, assumptions, and three recommended options (conservative, balanced, aggressive). Devin/Ira can you both review before EOD? Also include a short worksheet snippet so sales can tweak rps and tokens per request.
Devin: On it. I'll add a small spreadsheet CSV snippet for quick scenario runs.
Ira: Reviewing tonight. If we need regional guarantees, ping me about procurement lead times — eu-west 2-week minimal for guaranteed replacement hardware.
Sam: :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks — will post the draft in #sales-collab once reviewed.
